name: The Deity and Preexistence of Christ

objectives.text: Identify Jesus as God the Son
Name Jesus as the One through whom all things were made
Recall that Jesus lived with the Father before he was born in Bethlehem
Describe Gospel accounts in which people worshiped Jesus and he accepted their worship
Retell Jesus' words 'Before Abraham was, I am' and explain why his hearers tried to stone him
Explain the meaning of John 1:1 that the Word was with God and the Word was God
Contrast the eternal Son, who was not made, with everything that God created
Classify the titles of Christ that point to his deity, such as Lord, Son of God, Word, I AM, and God, using supporting verses
Analyze the 'I am' statements in the Gospel of John and explain how they echo God's name in Exodus
Explain how Scripture ascribes divine attributes and works to Christ, such as forgiving sins, knowing hearts, being unchanging, and judging the world
Analyze New Testament passages that apply Old Testament texts about the LORD directly to Jesus
Explain the Reformed teaching that the Son is eternally begotten of the Father and not made
Explain the Son's role as the agent through whom the Father created and now upholds all things
Analyze Old Testament appearances of the Angel of the LORD and evaluate the case that they reveal the preincarnate Son
Distinguish the Son's equality with the Father in essence from his distinction from the Father as a person
Explain how Philippians 2 and 2 Corinthians 8 assume the Son's existence in the form of God before his incarnation
Explain from the catechism why the Mediator must be true God
Construct a biblical case for the full deity of Christ using his names, attributes, works, and worship
Evaluate the Arian claim that 'there was when the Son was not' in light of Scripture
Analyze passages often cited against Christ's deity, such as 'firstborn of all creation' and 'the Father is greater than I', and interpret them in context
Defend the worship of Christ as worship that belongs to God alone
Explain how the Council of Nicaea's term homoousios, of one substance, answered Arianism and how the Westminster Confession restates it
Evaluate modern denials of Christ's deity, such as the rendering of John 1:1 as 'a god' and adoptionist views, using Scripture and the confessions

changes: Removed all Nicene Creed and Athanasian Creed citations because they are not in the library. Nicene content is now anchored to Westminster Confession of Faith 8.2 and 2.3, Belgic Confession Article 10, and Heidelberg Catechism Q33. Kept and reworded the real competencies (titles, I AM sayings, eternal generation, theophanies, agent of creation, Arian controversy, worship, homoousios) and tightened their verse anchors. Added objectives on divine attributes and works ascribed to Christ, Old Testament texts about the LORD applied to Jesus, the Son's distinction from the Father as a person, preexistence in Philippians 2 and 2 Corinthians 8, why the Mediator must be God, passages often cited against Christ's deity, and modern denials. Incarnation, offices, and atonement material is left to the sibling sub-topics.
